title: Property and job costing
goal: Build a cost ledger for one property and explain its budget vs actual and expected profit, with every number tied to an invoice.
concept_card: A vendor is who you pay; a project is where the cost belongs. Show actual paid, incurred unpaid, committed and forecast remaining separately. Every lender draw has four numbers: submitted, approved, funded and held back.
lesson_html:
A vendor is not a project. Every property and every plumbing job gets its own ID, address, owning company, purchase date, budget, lender and status. The plumber you pay is the vendor; the house is the project.

Types of property cost

  • Acquisition: purchase price and buying closing costs
  • Rehab: labor, materials, subcontractors, permits
  • Financing: loan interest, points, lender fees
  • Holding: property tax, insurance, utilities while you own it
  • Selling: closing costs on sale, agent commissions

Actual, committed, forecast. Actual is recorded (paid or billed). Committed is signed but not yet billed, like a contract or purchase order. Forecast to complete is your best estimate of what is still to come. Show all three separately.

Change orders change the budget. Record who approved them and update the forecast.

Lender draws. Track four numbers for each draw: what you submitted, what the lender approved, what actually arrived, and any holdback. Differences are not errors to ignore; each needs a reason.

Accounting treatment. For flips, rehab costs are usually added to the property's cost on the Balance Sheet rather than expensed right away. The CPA sets this policy. Write down their decision and follow it.
rule: Every cost on a property report links to an invoice, a bill or a closing statement.

qbo_steps.title: Turn on Projects
qbo_steps.html: Business → Projects (or the Projects menu). Available on Plus and Advanced. Create one project per property or job.

qbo_steps.title: Code every cost to the project
qbo_steps.html: On each bill, expense or check line, fill in the Customer/Project column. Also mark it billable if you re-bill it.

qbo_steps.title: Use classes or locations if the CPA wants them
qbo_steps.html: ⚙ → Account and settings → Advanced → Categories. Turn on class or location tracking.

qbo_steps.title: Set a budget
qbo_steps.html: ⚙ → Budgeting (Plus and Advanced). Create a budget by project or class.

qbo_steps.title: Run project reports
qbo_steps.html: Open a project to see its profitability tab, or Reports → Project profitability summary. Compare with Reports → Budget vs. Actuals.

scenario.text_html: Practice property TH-017 (made-up house). Sale price $385,000. Purchase $240,000. Rehab $62,000. Financing $11,500. Holding $4,300. Seller closing costs $7,700. Commissions $19,250.
scenario.ask: What is the profit on TH-017?
scenario.followup: The lender funded $36,000 of a $40,000 approved draw and kept $4,000 as retainage. How do you show that in the draw tracker?

quiz.q: A plumber invoices $1,800 for work at practice property TH-017. How is it coded?
quiz.why: The vendor is who you pay. The project is where the cost belongs.
quiz.followup: A change order adds $4,000 of tile. The budget line was $6,000 and $5,500 is already billed. What is the new variance?

options: A signed contract or purchase order not yet billed
A cost you hope to avoid
quiz.why: Committed means you're on the hook but no bill has arrived yet.

quiz.q: The lender approved a $40,000 draw but only $36,000 arrived. What is the $4,000?
options: A holdback, fee or disallowed cost that must be explained and tracked
quiz.why: Find out why: a holdback or retainage, a fee, or a cost the lender didn't allow. Record it in the draw tracker.

options: Your current best estimate of remaining cost
quiz.why: Budget minus actual is only a starting point. Use current information: bids, change orders, the site lead's estimate.

quiz.q: Who decides whether rehab costs are expensed or added to the property cost?
options: The CPA, written into the policy register
quiz.why: This is an accounting policy with tax effects. The CPA decides, and you document it.

task: Pick one real property. Build a cost list with every bill and closing-statement line, grouped by acquisition, rehab, financing, holding and selling. Compare to budget and explain the three biggest differences.
rubric: Every cost links to a document
Actual, committed and forecast shown separately
Budget vs actual difference explained for the top three lines
